description: The Marine Environment Information Portal (MEIS) gathers Korean marine environment data and statistics. Its home page summarises marine litter entering Korean seas (about 130,000 tonnes a year, with 2024 collection figures for shoreline, floating and seabed litter), sea water quality by coast (chemical oxygen demand averages for 2025), the national tidal flat area of 2,482 square kilometres split between the west and south coasts, 40 marine protected areas covering about 4,178 square kilometres (wetland, marine ecosystem, marine life and marine landscape protection areas), 91 protected marine species, marine radioactivity safety by sea area, and the automatic water quality monitoring network, whose stations from Incheon Songdo to Ulsan report water temperature, conductivity, pH and dissolved oxygen. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the portal is in Korean, the home page shows summaries, and the detailed data sits in sub-pages. Coverage is the coastal and marine waters of the Republic of Korea. It supports coastal environmental analysis around ports, power plant outfalls, tidal barrages and coastal defences, and nature-based coastal protection using tidal flats; related records are the Danish coastal data (Kystdata) and the Korean inland wetland data of the National Institute of Ecology.
